Projective texture mapping

A slide projector is a camera that shines its picture instead of recording one. Each vertex goes through the light's view and projection matrices and a bias, which gives the (s, t, depth, q) coordinate that textureProj divides by q. This page extends projectiveTexture with a choice of textures, colour, a floor and several objects to catch the slide, and shadows from a depth map rendered from the same projector.

What this page changes from projectiveTexture.js

  • The projection. The original computes 0.5*clip.xyz + 0.5 and hands it to textureProj, which divides by the third component, not by w. Here the vertex shader computes Bias * P_light * V_light * Model * position and textureProj divides by q = w. Points behind the projector have q < 0 and are switched off; otherwise they would receive a mirrored copy of the slide.
  • The projector's position. The original puts the projector at normalize(lightPosition), 1 unit from the origin, while its facing test uses the light's real position. Here one position is used for both.
  • The sampler. The original sets uTexture but the shader reads uTextureMap; it works only because unit 0 is the default. Here both names agree.
  • Shadows use a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 texture and a sampler2DShadow, with the same texture coordinate as the slide: the shadow map is itself a projective texture.
  • rotateY. The page uses rotate(angle, vec3(0, 1, 0)) rather than rotateY, as the light-view explorer does.
